components.css: .ds-rail{display:inline-flex;flex-direction:column;gap:1px;border-radius:10px 0 0 10px;box-shadow:0 12px 36px rgba(10,15,30,0.18);}.ds-rail-item{position:relative;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;width:54px;height:54px;background:var(--bg-navy,#003D7A);color:#fff;text-decoration:none;transition:background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1),color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1);}.ds-rail-item:first-child{border-top-left-radius:10px;}.ds-rail-item:last-child{border-bottom-left-radius:10px;}.ds-rail-item::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:0;top:0;bottom:0;width:3px;background:var(--accent-gold,#FFC107);transform:scaleY(0);transition:transform 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1);}.ds-rail-item:hover::before,.ds-rail-item:focus-visible::before{transform:scaleY(1);}.ds-rail-item:hover,.ds-rail-item:focus-visible{background:#0b2a52;color:var(--accent-gold,#FFC107);}.ds-rail-ico svg{width:22px;height:22px;display:block;}.ds-rail-pop{position:absolute;right:100%;top:0;height:54px;display:flex;align-items:center;margin-right:6px;padding:0 18px;background:var(--bg-navy,#003D7A);color:#fff;white-space:nowrap;font-family:var(--font-body,'IBM Plex Sans',system-ui,sans-serif);font-size:14px;font-weight:500;border-radius:8px;border-left:3px solid var(--accent-gold,#FFC107);box-shadow:0 12px 28px rgba(10,15,30,0.18);opacity:0;visibility:hidden;transform:translateX(8px);transition:opacity 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1),transform 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1),visibility 150ms;pointer-events:none;}.ds-rail-item:hover .ds-rail-pop,.ds-rail-item:focus-visible .ds-rail-pop{opacity:1;visibility:visible;transform:translateX(0);}

narrative.overview:
This is the desk of a Hong Kong trading house rendered as a website: white paper as the default ground, navy as the ink and the institutional mass, and a single gold thread that marks where the document is organised. It is not a SaaS landing page and not a machinery catalogue. A procurement engineer arriving with a part number should feel they have reached a counter that keeps records, not a funnel that keeps leads.

The system runs on restraint with one authored exception per screen. Sections breathe (96px of vertical air at desktop) while the content inside them stays dense and factual. Colour is budgeted rather than composed: roughly 70% white, 25% navy, 4% gold, 1% red, and the red appears on exactly one button per view. The serif carries authority, the sans carries information, the mono carries anything a buyer would copy.

Two things separate the implemented system from the original brand bible, and both are deliberate. First, form language: the bible demanded razor corners everywhere, but the shipped interface uses soft corners and light shadows on anything that floats, hovers, or is pressed. Second, the section label: the bible forbade gold as a fill, but the client asked for a solid gold block behind section labels, and the client's request wins.
keyCharacteristics: White-first surface; navy is mass, never a mood
Gold is a thread and a marker, never a mood either — one exception
Exactly one red button per view; red has no second job
Content sits on sharp-cornered cards; interface chrome is soft-cornered
Serif for authority, sans for information, mono for anything copyable
Bilingual by construction: every face chains IBM Plex Sans SC for 简体中文

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Exactly one #DC2626 button exists per view. A second red button is not an emphasis decision, it is a bug: demote it to secondary (navy outline) or to a link.

rules.name: The Gold Thread Rule
rules.body: Gold is a 1px rule, a 3px marker, a dot, or 11px letter-spaced type. It fills exactly one thing — the section label block — because the client asked for it. Any other gold fill is out of system.

rules.name: The Tint-Don't-Grey Rule
rules.body: Secondary text on navy is white at 70%, not grey. Secondary text on white is #6B7280. Never move a grey across grounds.

rules.name: The Measured-Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold type is checked against its ground, never eyeballed. Signal Gold (#FFC107) is for navy; Document Gold (#8A6508) is for paper. A new gold that has not been measured at 4.5:1 for its own background is not in the system.

rules.name: The Copyable-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: If a buyer might select it and paste it into an email — part number, phone, email, reference, registration number — it is IBM Plex Mono. If they would only read it, it is not.

rules.name: The One Weight Per Role Rule
rules.body: Each role owns one weight. Do not bold a word inside body copy for emphasis, do not colour a word, do not italicise. Emphasis is a different role or a different line.

rules.name: The Ruled-Paper Rule
rules.body: Sections are separated by a 1px Rule Grey border, not by empty space alone. The border is what makes a long scroll read as a document.

rules.name: The Reachable-Contact Rule
rules.body: Contact is never more than one gesture away at any width: header contacts at desktop, the fixed side rail above 980px, the burger menu below 768px, the footer everywhere. A layout change that removes a contact path without adding another is a regression.

rules.name: The Float-Earns-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow is permission to leave the page, not decoration. If the element is in the flow, it gets a border and a 4px lift instead.

rules.name: The One Grey-Black Rule
rules.body: Every shadow tints from rgba(10,15,30, α). Pure black shadows are out of system.

rules.name: The Sharp Content, Soft Chrome Rule
rules.body: If it holds the product's information, it has square corners. If it is a control, an overlay, or something that floats, it may round. When in doubt, the element is content.

rules.name: The Three-Step Rule (new work only)
rules.body: New components pick from 0, 8px, or pill. The 6 / 10 / 12 / 14px steps are legalised history, not an invitation — they stay where they are and nothing needs rework, but a new component reaching for a fourth radius is drifting.

rules.name: The One Curve Rule
rules.body: There is a single easing curve in this system. A new component that needs a different curve is asking for a different system.

dos: Do budget colour before composing it: ~70% white, ~25% navy, ~4% gold, ~1% red.
Do give every interactive content surface the same signal — 1px border to Trade Navy plus a 4px lift over 200ms.
Do use Document Gold (#8A6508) for gold type on white and Signal Gold (#FFC107) for gold type on navy. The two are not interchangeable.
Do set part numbers, phones, emails, references, and step numbers in IBM Plex Mono.
Do keep the section header exactly as built: gold block, 24px gold rule, serif lede beneath.
Do chain 'IBM Plex Sans SC' into any new font stack, or 简体中文 will break to a system face.
Do close every section with a 1px Rule Grey border.
donts: Don't put a second red button in a view.
Don't fill anything with gold except the section label block.
Don't add a shadow to an element that sits in the page flow; borders and lift carry content depth.
Don't introduce a radius outside 0, 8px, or pill in new components.
Don't grey out secondary text on navy — tint it from white at 70%.
Don't bold, colour, or italicise individual words for emphasis.
Don't use a neutral-black shadow; every shadow tints from rgba(10,15,30, α).
Don't remove a contact path at any breakpoint without replacing it with another.
